sahil: Quick FYI — after flipping FA v3 in canary we see an 8-12% tail-latency regression for small-batch short-seq traffic (bs=1-4, seq<=64) on A100-80GB. Not sure if it's kernel selection heuristics or a hidden workspace/padding cost.

mariam: Can you paste the perf run? numbers + command used?

sahil: ran our standard microbench: `./bench --model small-llm --device a100 --batch 1,2,4 --seq 8,32,64 --iters 200`. Summary: v2 p95 9.8ms -> v3 p95 10.8ms on seq=32 bs=1. throughput mostly same.

ryan: Hmm. v3 changed per-head tiling and adds an extra kernel for small seq fallback in some codepaths. That can add kernel launch overhead dominating at bs=1. Also check the workspace allocation path — v3 prefers larger prealloc granularity.

anya: Also worth checking continuous-batching behavior. If runtime batches requests differently after v3 (slightly delayed coalescing) that can bump tail. But your microbench was single-worker so probably kernel-level.

mariam: Do we have telemetry showing kernel_choice per-call? I want to see which variant was chosen for those shapes.

infra-bot: deploy: canary-flashattn-v3 rolled to 5% at 2025-11-03T14:10:23Z :rocket:

ryan: Telemetry TODOs: add tags `fa_variant` (v2|v3|fallback), `kernel_name`, `workspace_bytes_committed`, `launch_count`, and `seq_len_bucket`. Also collect `kernel_time_us` and `total_inference_us`.

anya: Short patch snippet for kernel selection interface I propose — small and backward compatible:
```
// signature in runtime/kernel_selector.h
using KernelDecision = struct {
  string kernel_name;
  size_t workspace_bytes;
  bool requires_padding;
};
KernelDecision choose_attention_kernel(const ModelShape&, const HardwareProfile&, const RuntimeHints&);
```
This way selector returns both name and workspace so caller can precommit telemetry and fallback easily.

sahil: Love it. Also add a `should_fallback` fast flag to avoid re-running heuristics in hot path.

mariam: For experiments: 1) reproduce microbench with perf counters (nsight) to confirm kernel launch / memcpy time; 2) force v3 to pick v2 kernel via env flag to confirm regression source; 3) run per-thread workspace sizing tweak (reduce prealloc granularity) to see effect.

ryan: I can do (2) today — adding `FA_FORCE_KERNEL=v2` env carveout and re-run. If regression goes away -> kernel decision. If not -> workspace or batching.

anya: I'll instrument selector to emit `kernel_name` and `workspace_bytes` to our metrics pipeline (low-cardinality) so we can slice by model/seq/bs.

infra-bot: perf-job: 1930456798 started by ryan on canary (A100) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mariam: One more note — ensure we log `padding_applied` boolean. v3 has different pad-to multiples which could increase memory traffic on small seq.

sahil: Ownering: ryan -> reproduce + forced-kernel run; anya -> selector telemetry patch + small API; mariam -> nsight microprofile and workspace/alloc traces. Re-check in ~24h.

ryan: If this is a kernel-launch penalty we could consider merging tiny-seq fast-path that inlines the shortest path (single-kernel) for seq<=32, bs<=2. But prefer data first.

anya: Agreed. Also we should add a canary rollout that prefers v2 for short-seq routes as a mitigation if needed.

mariam: Sounds good. tagging @infra to widen rollout knob exposure. :eyes:

sahil: Thanks team. Will post follow-up with perf artifacts and nsight captures. :thumbsup:
